name: FlashInfer: Efficient and Customizable Attention Engine for LLM Inference Serving
problem: Serving attention is not one problem: paged KV layouts, variable batch, head counts and context lengths each stress a different part of the memory hierarchy, so a single hardcoded attention kernel leaves large amounts of performance on the table across the workload distribution.
mechanism: An attention ENGINE rather than a kernel. Three components: (1) block-sparse and composable KV formats so heterogeneous KV-cache layouts are expressed declaratively and memory access stays coalesced with less redundancy; (2) a customisable JIT-compiled attention template generated per configuration; (3) a load-balanced scheduling algorithm that adapts to request dynamism while remaining compatible with CUDAGraph's static-shape requirement.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claims (abstract), against state-of-the-art LLM serving solutions and compiler backends: 29-69% inter-token-latency reduction on the LLM serving benchmark vs compiler backends; 28-30% latency reduction for long-context inference; 13-17% speedup for parallel generation. These are percentage latency reductions with named baseline class, not bare multipliers.
